text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today as the stock continues a broader two-week decline despite solid refining conditions. The company reported quarterly earnings and a leadership change on November 3rd, but the market's reaction has been cautious — the stock is down 10% over two weeks even as U.S. oil prices sit near $103 per barrel and U.S. refineries operate at a healthy 92.8% capacity, conditions that typically support refiner profitability.

The caution likely reflects broader skepticism about Big Oil guidance going forward. Market commentary from late October flagged that while energy earnings are strong right now, investor focus is shifting to what companies will say about future demand and returns — especially with the possibility of a Democratic Congress that could prioritize renewable energy over traditional oil and gas infrastructure.
